summary: Three-tier token model (primitive, semantic, component) with tier purposes, sample CSS per tier, dark mode as semantic override, naming pattern, categories, file layout, flat-token migration, DTCG JSON shape.
mech: Primitives hold raw values only; semantic tokens may reference only primitives; component tokens reference semantic tokens; verify no component rule points at a raw value or primitive.
Implement dark mode as a block that overrides only semantic tokens; primitives and component tokens stay unchanged; verify the dark block contains no new raw values.
Name tokens category-item-variant-state; migrate flat per-component hex tokens by extracting primitives, aliasing semantics, then pointing component tokens at semantics.

summary: Sample primitive scales: gray and one brand hue ramps 50-950, status hues, 4px-based spacing ramp, type size, leading, weight and tracking scales, radius, shadow, duration and z-index ladders.
mech: Build every scale as a stepped ramp on one base unit (spacing on 4px steps); verify each spacing value used in output is a ramp member.
Define named z-index layers in ascending order dropdown, sticky, modal, popover, tooltip so overlay stacking is predictable; verify no ad hoc z-index numbers.
Alias motion durations as fast, normal, slow from a raw duration ramp so components cite intent, not milliseconds.

summary: Semantic color roles paired with foreground counterparts (surface, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, status, border, ring), spacing, type and interaction aliases, dark overrides, good-versus-bad usage example.
mech: Give every fill role a paired foreground token (primary and primary-foreground); verify each pair meets contrast in both light and dark themes.
Component styles must use semantic roles, never primitives directly; flag any component rule citing a raw ramp step such as gray-50.
Dark theme overrides surfaces, muted, secondary, accent, border and input roles only; brand and status roles keep values unless contrast fails.

summary: Component-tier token sets for button, input, card, badge, alert, dialog and table, each aliasing semantic roles for variant fills, hover and active, focus, error, disabled, sizing and shape.
mech: For each component list tokens per variant and per state (bg, fg, hover-bg, active-bg, border) aliased to semantic roles; verify every declared state has a token.
Input tokens must cover placeholder, focus border and ring, error border and text, disabled fill and text; a missing one means an unspecified state.
Size variants (sm, default, lg) change only padding, height and font tokens; colors stay shared so variants never fork the palette.

summary: Interactive state table with triggers, state precedence order, transition timings, focus-ring spec, disabled, loading and error treatments, variant patterns via local custom properties, contrast minima, ARIA markup.
mech: When states overlap resolve by precedence disabled > loading > active > focus > hover > default; verify each interactive component documents all six.
Focus ring is a two-layer outline (background-colored offset then ring color) on focus-visible; error state swaps ring to error color; verify ring contrast at least 3:1.
Never signal state by color alone: add icon or text; error text sits below field with icon, clears on valid input; loading sets aria-busy plus screen-reader text.

summary: Spec tables for button, input, card, badge, alert, dialog and table: variants with use cases, size ladders, per-state treatments, anatomy sketches, dialog widths, table alignment and row densities.
mech: Map button variants to action rank: filled for primary, tonal for secondary, outline or ghost for tertiary, link for navigation, destructive only for dangerous actions.
Table cells: left-align text, right-align numbers and row actions, center status badges; offer compact, default and comfortable row heights.
Dialog anatomy: header with title and close, scrollable content, footer actions with cancel before confirm; dialog goes full width minus margins on mobile.

summary: Maps semantic tokens to a utility-CSS framework: space-separated HSL variables for light and dark, config color mapping, radius derived from one variable, component classes, duration tokens, dark toggle.
mech: Store color tokens as bare channel values so utilities can apply opacity modifiers; derive smaller radii from one base radius variable by subtraction.
Hover on filled buttons is the same role at reduced opacity; dark mode toggles a root class, initialized from the system color-scheme preference.
Stale risk: config-file setup reflects an older framework major version; verify against the installed version before porting.

summary: Sixteen named aesthetic direction recipes (color seed ranges, type family, shape and depth, signature, imagery, do-not-use contexts), three design dials with presets, per-direction motion envelopes; all self-labelled unverified.
mech: Direction = color seed ranges, type family, radius and depth, one signature, imagery, do-not-use contexts; when adapting, change at least two fields and write why.
Check each direction's do-not-use list against the product (trust finance or health, weak phones, long text, children, elderly); any match vetoes it; one direction per product.
Set three 1-10 dials (variance, motion, density) from the product; density picks the spacing range; scale motion duration by distance, element size and task importance.

summary: Visual heuristics by screen archetype with exception-note format, first-glance check, hero weight, color proportion, restraint budget, card discipline, conditional dark mode, scaled motion, identity templates, anti-generic audit.
mech: Classify screen archetype first; hero and color-proportion rules apply only to showcase screens; skipping a rule needs a one-line exception: rule, evidence-backed reason, substitute.
Restraint budget per screen: one gradient, one blur layer, one focal animation, one accent hue, four type sizes, three weights; delete any effect whose removal loses nothing.
A redesign counts as distinct only with written change in two of typography, layout composition, component relationships, beyond surface color, shadow or radius.

summary: Visual token set with may-use and may-not-use rules per token (color roles, type scale, spacing, elevation, radius, motion, breakpoints), component recipes with states, presentation plan, palette table, per-screen blueprint templates.
mech: Every token carries a may-use and may-not-use rule; components cite token names only, raw hex appears once in a palette table with measured contrast and evidence label.
Text roles: primary, secondary and meaningful tertiary text at least 4.5:1 against their surface; non-text cues 3:1; disabled text carries a one-line reason; never below 12px.
Per-screen blueprint: archetype and anchor, one row per element listing tier and tokens plus hit area, hero clearance, all states, reflow at three widths and largest font.

summary: Four-step Devanagari verification (glyph coverage by family and build, explicit fallback stack, five render checks, honest evidence label), companion font list, subset snapshot table, general type rules.
mech: Never infer script support from a font name: check the exact build's Unicode block and shaping tables, else add an explicit script fallback to the stack.
Render real mixed strings and check conjuncts, vowel signs, line height 1.5-1.6 body, clipping inside buttons, chips and inputs, and mixed-script baseline; unrendered means not-tested.
Mobile body at least 16px, nothing under 12px, line 35-60 characters mobile and 60-75 desktop, tabular numerals for data; no negative tracking, caps or italics on Devanagari.

summary: Table of 74 named heading and body font pairings with mood keywords and best-for contexts, including per-script pairings, prefaced by a warning not to assume Devanagari support from font names.
mech: Pairing choice is keyword matching: product context and mood words against each pairing's mood and best-for columns; at most two families; single-family pairings rely on weight contrast.
Non-Latin scripts get script-native families; 'subset not listed in snapshot' means unverified, not absent; run a coverage check and add a fallback before using.
Pairing logic contrasts a display face (serif, geometric or condensed) with a neutral readable body face; trust or accessibility contexts favour hyperlegible or plain sans.

summary: Matrix of 50 named visual styles, each with suitable contexts and do-not-use contexts, plus a short selection method; points to supplemental and deprecated styles in the full table.
mech: Pick a style from product type, audience and task; then check its do-not-use list; any accessibility or performance veto removes it; one style across the whole product.
Recurring vetoes: effect-heavy styles (glass, 3D, motion-led, neumorphic) excluded for accessibility-critical, low-end devices, dense data; loud styles excluded for finance, health, government.
Platform design systems fit only products living on that platform; using one elsewhere imports conventions users will not expect.

summary: Motion durations scaled by distance, element size and task importance, web motion tiers with easings, performance and accessibility rules, and a chart picker mapping data shape to chart with thresholds.
mech: Scale duration by distance, size and importance (press about 100ms, sheet 300-450ms, one hero moment per screen); animate transform and opacity only; exit 60-70% of enter.
Animations must be interruptible and never block input; reduced-motion turns entrances and shimmer static; motion never outranks accessibility, frame budget or task clarity.
Pick chart by data question; fallbacks: under 4 points a stat card, over 15 categories a table, over 5 slices a bar; add table, insight line, non-color encoding.

summary: Table of 192 product categories each mapped to a page pattern, two priority styles, colour mood, typography mood, key effects and an avoid list; rendered from the reasoning table.
mech: Category drives five choices: page pattern, style pair, colour mood, type mood, effects; the avoid column vetoes trust-breaking looks (playful in finance, neon or heavy motion in health).
Avoid lists also name missing function (hidden fees, no search, no status, color-only indicators); port these as functional veto checks, not visual picks.
Conflicts with style-matrix: low-contrast soft styles prescribed for health and calm categories that style-matrix vetoes for critical accessibility; check style vetoes after lookup.

summary: Worked examples: placement before decoration, literal versus rethought layouts for two sample product requests, a micro-change answer format, a missing-reference gate with resume line, honest evidence-label wording.
mech: Place the primary action where the thumb reaches (bottom, full width, 48-56px) before styling; a well-styled element in the wrong place still fails.
For a request listing N separate tools, compare literal (N pages), rethought (one workspace with auto-detect plus one-tap override) and zero-step options; pick with reasons.
Evidence wording: claim tool-verified only with the command shown; without a render run the verdict is spec-approved, render-unverified; never say passed or approved.

summary: Version history of the source skill from v11 to v18 rev 3: audit fixes, architecture split, size router, scorecard layers, evidence labels, verify-first script rule, and historical untested-status notes.
mech: Recompute every tool-cited number in examples by re-running the tool; the source found its own 'verified' contrast example wrong this way.
Keep untested status explicit: the source states the method was never field-tested on a real requirements document.

summary: 32 mobile-app UX rules (accessibility, forms, touch, navigation, feedback, performance, animation, type, safe areas, theming) each with description, do, don't, good and bad code, severity.
mech: Each row is a checkable do/don't with severity; audit a mobile screen by walking rows and citing violated issue plus severity, critical first.
Verify icon-only buttons and inputs expose accessible labels, targets meet minimum size and spacing, every gesture action has a visible button alternative, modals offer escape.
Forms: validate on blur or submit not per keystroke, correct keyboard type, next-field focus, password reveal, allow paste and password managers; respect safe areas and reduced motion.

summary: 25 data-shape rows mapping to best and secondary chart types with when-to-use, when-not, volume thresholds, colour guidance, accessibility risk, notes, fallback, library, interaction level.
mech: Choose chart from the data question, then test its when-not column (too few points, too many series or categories) and switch to the named fallback.
Volume thresholds pick rendering: vector graphics for small sets, canvas plus downsampling above about a thousand points, aggregate beyond; source's own numbers.
Every chart needs non-color encoding (line styles, patterns, direct labels), a visible data table plus summary, and keyboard focus that reveals hover values.

summary: 192 product-type rows each prescribing a full semantic palette in hex (primary, secondary, accent with on-colours, background, foreground, card, muted, border, destructive, ring) plus a mood note.
mech: A palette is a set of semantic roles each with a paired on-colour; derive roles from mood and category, then check every pair's contrast before use.
When an accent fails contrast against its on-colour, darken it and record the original value; the table notes 56 such adjustments.
Variety risk: about half the primaries fall in blue hues and one blue plus one violet recur across 33 rows; table-driven palettes converge.
